hero.eyebrow: A flashcard app for learning that lasts
hero.title:
Study quietly.
Remember everything.
hero.lede: JustFlip! is a spaced-repetition flashcard app for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. Curate your decks on the desktop, review them on the go, and let an SM-2-inspired engine surface the right card at the right moment.
hero.floatPillText: New — generate decks with your favorite AI agent
devices.title:
One library.
Three companions.
devices.kicker: Capture and curate on the Mac. Review on the iPhone over morning coffee. Annotate on the iPad in the margins. iCloud keeps every card, every interval and every streak in perfect sync — without ever asking you to think about it.
devices.stageLabel: Image · iPhone, iPad & Mac with synced decks
devices.macosDesc: Import .flashcard archives by drag-and-drop, manage interests, edit cards in a dedicated editor.
devices.ipadosDesc: A wide canvas for long-form review sessions with Pencil-friendly typography and split view.
devices.iosDesc: Daily reviews, hands-free spoken decks, and progress tracked card-by-card.
ai.title: Let the AI write the deck.
ai.kicker: Two ways to create decks — full rich-content cards with agentic coding tools, or simple text-only sets directly in ChatGPT.
ai.terminalAria: Terminal demo of generating a flashcard deck with an AI agent
ai.richDesc: Generate decks with images, audio, and Markdown formatting. Requires an agentic coding tool like Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode.
ai.textDesc: Quick text-only flashcards — no images or audio. Use the JustFlip GPT in ChatGPT, or copy the same prompt into Claude or Gemini.
study.title: A library you can swipe through.
study.kicker: Browse decks as a calm, editorial list — or enter a focused review and judge each card with a Tinder-style swipe. Right for good, left for again, up for easy. The flow stays in your hand.
algorithm.title:
A patient algorithm.
Five states. Lasting recall.
algorithm.kicker: JustFlip! runs a refined SM-2 engine across five learning states. Cards travel through unseen, learning, reviewing, relearning and graduated, each with its own interval and ease. Urgency tells you what is most worth your time today.
algorithm.unseenDesc: Never studied — ready for first contact.
algorithm.learningDesc: Minutes to a day. Fresh memory taking shape.
algorithm.reviewingDesc: Days to weeks. The interval grows by ease.
algorithm.relearningDesc: Forgotten? Back to short intervals, gently.
algorithm.formulaNote: Ease grows on easy, settles on good, and contracts on hard or again — never below 1.3.
science.title:
Not just flipping cards.
A proven way to remember.
science.kicker: Decades of memory research — popularized in the bestselling book Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning — point to one conclusion: we remember by retrieving, not rereading, and by spacing practice over time. JustFlip! turns that science into a daily habit.
science.chartLabel: Chart comparing how memory fades after a single cram versus spaced review
science.chartNote: Each review lifts recall and flattens the curve of forgetting.
science.retrievalDesc: Every card asks you to pull the answer from memory before you flip — that effort is what makes it stick.
science.spacingTitle: Let a little forgetting work for you
science.spacingDesc: Reviews return just as memory starts to fade, when each repetition does the most good — the SM-2 engine's quiet job.
science.interleaveDesc: Shuffling topics in one session feels harder — and builds memory that lasts far longer than studying in blocks.
science.difficultyDesc: Judging each card Again, Hard, Good or Easy keeps reviews honestly challenging — the kind of effort that deepens learning.
science.quote: “Learning is deeper and more durable when it's effortful.”
science.quoteAttr: — Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
markdown.title: Cards that read like essays.
markdown.kicker: Define your cards in rich Markdown — headings, lists, code blocks, inline math, images and links. JustFlip! renders them with editorial typography so a card can be a one-line cue or a small piece of scholarship.
markdown.label: Image · Markdown-rich card definition
audio.title: Decks that speak.
audio.kicker: Let your cards read themselves out loud while you walk, cook, or drive. A Live Activity on your Lock Screen keeps the playback in sight — a small, golden invitation to five minutes of practice.
glance.title: Your day, at a glance.
glance.kicker: Open your Mac and JustFlip! greets you with today's review — what's due, what's new, and a single warm tap to begin. On iPhone and iPad, Lock Screen and Home Screen widgets keep your due count, your streak and your week's rhythm a glance away — so the next five minutes are never more than a look from where you already are.
glance.stageLabel: The macOS today-review panel beside iPhone Lock Screen and Home Screen widgets
glance.todayDesc: The Mac welcomes you with today's queue — cards due and cards new — and starts the session in a single tap.
glance.lockDesc: Cards due and your running streak sit quietly on the Lock Screen, nudging you toward five honest minutes.
glance.homeTitle: A week at a size that fits
glance.homeDesc: A Home Screen widget charts your week, so progress stays in view between everything else you opened the phone for.
watch.title: On your wrist, too.
watch.kicker: Feel the tap, glance down, rate the card — the same spaced-repetition engine, three inches from your pulse. Turn the Digital Crown to keep reading; a firm press marks it Again, Hard, Good or Easy. No phone required.
watch.stageAria: Video — reviewing a flashcard deck on Apple Watch
theme.title:
Dark by candlelight.
Light by morning.
theme.kicker: JustFlip! respects the system. Switch from a deep, scholarly dark to a soft parchment light — the gold and slate stay true at any hour.
access.title: Learning, for every learner.
access.kicker: JustFlip! is built to work with the tools people rely on — so a deck is just as usable with a screen reader, at any text size, by ear, or in your own language.
access.voiceDesc: Navigate every deck with VoiceOver — cards, controls and each learning state are clearly labeled.
access.speakDesc: Text-to-speech reads your cards aloud for eyes-free, low-vision and dyslexia-friendly study.
access.typeDesc: Respects your system text size, so cards and layout scale up without ever breaking.
access.contrastDesc: The five learning states are set apart by label and position — never color alone — with a dedicated high-contrast mode in the works.
access.langDesc: The whole app — and this very page — is localized into nine languages.
access.langList: English · Deutsch · Español · Français · Italiano · Português · 日本語 · 한국어 · Čeština

prompt.metaTitle: JustFlip! AI Prompt for Claude and Gemini
prompt.metaDescription: Describe the deck you want, copy one prompt into Claude, Gemini, or any chat AI, and get an importable JustFlip .flashcards file back.
prompt.eyebrow: For Claude, Gemini and any chat AI
prompt.title:
Describe it.
Get a JustFlip deck.
prompt.lede: Type what you want to learn. We bundle your request with the JustFlip build instructions so any chat AI returns an importable .flashcards file. ChatGPT has a ready-made JustFlip GPT — Claude Projects and Gemini Gems can't be shared publicly, so this page gives you the same instructions as one copyable prompt.
prompt.panelText: You only write your topic or notes. The button adds the technical build instructions behind them — you can expand and read those anytime. Nothing is sent anywhere; the prompt is just copied to your clipboard.
prompt.editorTitle: Describe the deck you want to study.
prompt.editorKicker: Write a topic, paste your notes, an article or a lecture transcript. When you copy, your text is bundled with the JustFlip build instructions — paste the whole thing into a new Claude or Gemini chat.
prompt.techSummary: Show the instructions added to your request
prompt.techHint: read-only · added automatically when you copy
prompt.editorNote: After the AI saves the .flashcards file, download it and open it with JustFlip to import the deck.
prompt.step1Text: Type your topic or paste your notes in the box above, then hit Copy full prompt.
prompt.step2Text: Open Claude or Gemini in a new chat and paste. Your request and the build instructions go together.
prompt.step3Text: The AI returns a .flashcards file. Download it and open it with JustFlip.
prompt.copySuccess: Full prompt copied — paste it into Claude or Gemini.
prompt.copyFail: Could not copy automatically. Expand the instructions, select the text and copy it manually.
skill.metaTitle: JustFlip! Rich decks from your AI coding agent
skill.metaDescription: Install one skill, point your AI coding agent at a folder, and get back a rich JustFlip deck with images, audio and Markdown — no copy-pasting.
skill.eyebrow: For Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode & any coding agent
skill.title:
A folder of files.
A rich deck back.
skill.lede: The AI Prompt page makes quick text-only cards in any chat. This is the other way: add one skill to your AI coding agent and it builds full JustFlip decks — with images, audio and Markdown — straight from the files on your disk. No copy-pasting, no hand-written JSON.
skill.promptCta: Just text? Use the prompt page
skill.panelText: A chat AI returns a text-only .flashcards file. Your coding agent can read local images, audio and notes, so it returns a .flashcards.zip bundle with the media already attached — ready to open in JustFlip.
skill.installTitle: Add the JustFlip skill to your agent.
skill.installKicker: One command installs the justflip-create-flashcards skill into any agent that supports skills.sh. Run it once in your project, then just ask in plain language.
skill.pointImagesText: Attach local photos and diagrams to either side of a card.
skill.pointAudioText: Bundle pronunciation clips and spoken-form hints for TTS.
skill.pointMarkdownText: Rich formatting, code blocks and LaTeX, rendered natively in-app.
skill.demoTitle: Point it at a folder. Ask in plain words.
skill.demoKicker: Say you have a folder of mushroom photos named after each species. Ask your agent to turn the file names into questions and the photos into answers — it reads the folder, builds the deck and packages the images for you.
skill.demoPrompt: This folder contains images of mushrooms. Take the file names as the question text and the mushroom image as the answer. Prepare the flashcards deck.
skill.demoStep2: Turning each file name into a question
skill.demoStep3: Attaching each photo as the answer (a_image)
skill.fileMeta: Open with JustFlip to import · 6 cards
skill.resultLabel: The deck, as it lands in JustFlip — file name on the front, photo on the back.
skill.step1Text: Run npx skills add DanielCech/JustFlip-Skills once in your project.
skill.step2Text: Point the agent at your files and describe the deck you want — in plain language.
skill.step3Text: It writes a .flashcards.zip. Open it with JustFlip and the deck is in.
learning.metaTitle: JustFlip! Why classic studying is a myth — and how to learn effectively
learning.metaDescription: Highlighting and rereading feel productive, but the memory fades fast. Learn how retrieval practice, spaced repetition and interleaving — the science behind Make It Stick — help you remember for good, and how JustFlip! puts them to work.
learning.title:
Classic studying is a myth.
Learn what actually works.
learning.lede: Remember the sleepless nights spent highlighting textbooks, or reading the same notes over and over? Most of us grew up believing that the more time we spend passively going over the material, the deeper it sinks in. We have news that may surprise you — and will most likely come as a relief: science shows that this is not how effective learning works at all.
learning.panelText: In the landmark book Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning, researchers showed that our intuition often betrays us when we study. This is the story of why we learn the wrong way — and how JustFlip! lets you change it today.
learning.illusionTitle: A trap called the illusion of knowing.
learning.illusionKicker: The greatest enemy of effective learning is your own brain. Read a text three or four times in a row and it starts to feel like familiar ground. The information seems known — and you convince yourself you've mastered it.
learning.illusionP1: Experts call this the illusion of knowing. We are simply poor judges of how much we've actually learned. The real test comes only at the moment we have to pull the information out of our head without a hint. And that's exactly where we so often fail.
learning.testingTitle: Self-testing: the most honest mirror of your memory.
learning.testingKicker: So how do you escape the trap? The authors of Make It Stick offer an unambiguous answer: the best tool for learning is self-testing.
learning.testingP1: When you actively try to recall an answer to a question, you force your brain to work. It isn't just a knowledge check — the very act of retrieving a memory changes the structure of your brain and strengthens neural connections. Self-testing is the most honest method there is: it exposes your gaps immediately.
learning.testingP2: For it to work perfectly, two key principles need to join in. Together they are known as spaced repetition.
learning.forgetTitle: Review just as you begin to forget
learning.forgetDesc: It sounds paradoxical, but memory is strengthened most when you recall a fact at the exact moment it starts slipping away. That desirable effort is what writes knowledge into long-term memory.
learning.interleaveDesc: Instead of drilling one narrow topic for an hour, it's far better to interleave subjects and areas. Your brain has to keep switching and re-establishing context — which leads to results that last.
learning.honestTitle: Learning that works hurts a little
learning.honestText: We won't promise miracles. JustFlip! is no magic wand that pours knowledge into your head without work — proper learning takes effort. It's completely normal to feel a bit frustrated at first, mildly “confused”, or like you're going slowly. That is not a sign of failure — it's the moment your brain is genuinely rewiring. Forgetting is natural and can't be stopped, but with these methods you'll keep many times more in memory. You'll see the real difference within a few days.
learning.practiceKicker: We built JustFlip! precisely to help you apply the lessons of Make It Stick in everyday life — without having to invent your own system for when and what to review.
learning.algoDesc: JustFlip! implements the proven SM-2 algorithm with our own refinements. The app computes the ideal moment to show each card — you see it exactly when you're starting to forget it.
learning.reviewDesc: Learning is about consistency. The integrated review panel helps you keep studying as an active daily habit — you always know exactly how much work awaits, and you watch your progress grow.
learning.aiDesc: No time to write cards by hand? The AI tools built into JustFlip! help you prepare quality study material from virtually any source — lecture notes, an article, or your own notes.
learning.ctaLede: Give your brain the right impulse, embrace the healthy effort, and watch how quickly your knowledge grows. Download JustFlip! today and feel the power of science-backed learning for yourself.

Nice to meet you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lede: This policy explains what information JustFlip does not collect, what limited technical data may be processed by third-party services, and how privacy is handled across the app.
privacy.intro1: Daniel Čech ("I", "me", or "my") operates the JustFlip mobile application (the "Application"). This Privacy Policy explains how I collect, use, and disclose information when you use the Application.
privacy.noCollectTitle: 1. Personal Data I Do Not Collect
privacy.noCollect1: 1.1. I do not require account registration.
privacy.noCollect2: 1.2. I do not collect, store, or have access to your name, email address, password, or any personal identifiers.
privacy.noCollect3: 1.3. Your app data (flashcards, images) is stored on your device and in your personal Apple iCloud storage. I cannot access this data.
privacy.noCollect4: 1.4. If you enable iCloud, your app data is synchronized across your devices through Apple's iCloud (CloudKit) service. This synchronization is operated entirely by Apple under Apple's own privacy policy. I have no access to your iCloud data and no control over Apple's sync service.
privacy.thirdPartyLead: To improve the performance and reliability of the Application, I use third-party analytics and monitoring tools. These tools may collect certain non-personal, technical information automatically:
privacy.thirdParty1:
2.1. Google Analytics for Firebase
I use this service to understand how users interact with the Application (e.g., which features are used most frequently). This data is anonymized and aggregated.
privacy.thirdParty2:
2.2. Firebase Crashlytics
I use this service to monitor app stability and collect crash reports. If the Application crashes, Crashlytics collects technical details about the crash (e.g., device type, operating system version, and the state of the app at the time of the crash) to help me fix the issue.
privacy.thirdParty3:
2.3. RevenueCat
I use RevenueCat to manage in-app purchases and subscriptions. When you make or restore a purchase, RevenueCat processes a randomly generated app-user identifier and transaction data (such as the product purchased and purchase status) to validate your access to paid features. It does not receive your name or Apple ID.
privacy.children1: 3.1. Since I do not collect any personal data, the Application does not knowingly collect or solicit personal information from anyone, including children under the age of 13.
